profile.name: Fang Xu
profile.description: Fang Xu is a biomedical engineering undergraduate at ShanghaiTech University, working on neural interfaces, computational design, and machine learning for biomedical signals.
bio: I am an undergraduate student in [Biomedical Engineering](https://bme.shanghaitech.edu.cn/bme_en/) at [ShanghaiTech University](https://www.shanghaitech.edu.cn/en/), advised by [Prof. Ze Xiong](https://bme.shanghaitech.edu.cn/bme_en/2021/0326/c8252a1073789/page.htm) and affiliated with the [Wireless and Smart Bio-electronics (WiSe) Lab](https://xiong-group.com/).

Previously, I was fortunate to work with [Prof. Sung Il Park](https://bme.shanghaitech.edu.cn/bme_en/2021/0326/c8252a1087808/page.htm) in the [Park Lab](https://parklab.bme.shanghaitech.edu.cn/) at [ShanghaiTech University](https://www.shanghaitech.edu.cn/en/) on adaptive wireless power transfer and flexible optoelectronic devices for optogenetics. I expect to receive my B.Eng. in Biomedical Engineering in July 2027.

I am mainly interested in **automated design** of neural interfaces and **machine learning** for biomedical signals, particularly brain-organoid electrode interfaces and cross-subject EEG emotion recognition.

research.title: Neural interfaces
research.description: Computational design of flexible electrode scaffolds for brain organoids, bringing together geometry, routing, fabrication, and finite-element evaluation.

research.title: Machine learning for biosignals
research.description: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition using multi-expert models, signal features, functional connectivity, and depression-aware fusion.

research.title: Wireless bioelectronics
research.description: Adaptive wireless power transfer and flexible optoelectronic systems for optogenetic interfaces, from circuit design to microfabrication.

news.text: Completed an investment-research internship focused on semiconductors and embodied intelligence.
Our paper on single-image 3D reconstruction of painted potteries was published in npj Heritage Science.
Joined the WiSe Lab at ShanghaiTech University as an undergraduate researcher.

projects.title: ARISE · Organoid electrode-interface design
projects.description: An integrated design-and-simulation workbench for organoid electrode interfaces.
bullets: Independently developed a pipeline from GDS scaffold geometries to electrode placement, graph-based routing, constrained interconnect selection, and four-sided pad layouts.
Integrated batch geometry checks, coverage analysis, and COMSOL evaluation of contact pressure, strain, and material fraction; fabricated flexible electrode prototypes with Xingming Wen.

projects.title: DREAM · Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition
projects.highlight: Gold Prize · 11th National Undergraduate Biomedical Engineering Innovation and Design Competition
projects.description: A depression-aware, multi-expert EEG emotion-recognition pipeline.
bullets: Independently developed and optimized models for 30-channel, 10-second EEG segments, combining EEGNet-based spatiotemporal modeling, statistical features, MODMA-derived priors, and SEED-based stimulus prototypes.
Designed functional-connectivity residual fusion, constrained within-subject ranking, and targeted boundary re-ranking; worked with the team on the final inference pipeline.

projects.title: Adaptive wireless power transfer for optogenetics
projects.description: AI-guided antenna control for a 13.56 MHz wireless power system.
bullets: Developed an antenna-control strategy using RSSI and animal-posture features to predict optical power at an implanted receiver and select transmitting antennas in real time.
Contributed to antenna impedance matching and antenna-array scanning and switching logic to address unstable power delivery.

projects.title: Flexible wireless optoelectronic devices
projects.description: Device design, microfabrication, assembly, and encapsulation for wireless optoelectronic interfaces.
bullets: Independently completed the single-channel device workflow on flexible Cu/polyimide substrates, including photolithography, wet etching, micro-LED soldering, testing, and PDMS/parylene encapsulation.
Collaborated with lab colleagues on the design, fabrication, soldering, testing, and encapsulation of four-channel devices.

projects.title: Ultrasound image analysis: classical methods to foundation models
projects.role: Course project · Instructor: Prof. Xuejun Qian
bullets: Compared four segmentation strategies and three classifiers on 120 breast ultrasound images with 36 radiomic features using stratified five-fold cross-validation. BUSAT+SVM achieved 89.2% accuracy; BUSAT+random forest achieved an AUC of 0.940.

Benchmarked SAM2/MedSAM prompted segmentation and frozen foundation-model encoders for classification; BiomedCLIP+SVM achieved an AUC of 0.935. Also analyzed eight neck ultrasound acquisitions for carotid-artery quantification.

projects.title: Single-image 3D reconstruction of painted pottery
projects.role: Research project · Advisor: Prof. Dongdong Tu
bullets: Contributed to data collection and experiments comparing diffusion-based novel-view synthesis and feedforward 3D reconstruction methods.
Benchmarked seven reconstruction methods and evaluated appearance and geometry using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, Chamfer distance, and IoU.

projects.title: Single-slope ADC for EEG acquisition
projects.role: Course project · Instructor: Prof. Xiaochun Lai
bullets: Designed and simulated a single-slope ADC module for an EEG acquisition front end in Cadence Virtuoso.
Designed a folded-cascode OTA, sample-and-hold circuit, non-overlap clock, and linear ramp generator, focusing on circuit precision and timing.

projects.title: ECG acquisition and real-time waveform display
bullets: Designed the PCB and coordinated fabrication for an ECG front end with an instrumentation amplifier, two gain stages, and a 50 Hz notch filter.
Programmed an Arduino UNO for sampling and PC communication, integrating the analog front end with real-time waveform display.
